q: Hartman-Grobman theorem states that near a hyperbolic equilibrium x* of ẋ = f(x):
opts: The nonlinear system is globally topologically conjugate to its linearization
The flow is locally topologically conjugate to the linear flow ẋ = Df(x*)x
The system has a Lyapunov function equal to the quadratic form from Df
Stability is determined by the nonlinear terms
exp: Hartman-Grobman: near a hyperbolic fixed point (no eigenvalue with zero real part), the nonlinear flow is locally topologically conjugate (homeomorphic) to the linearization—the qualitative picture is the same.
